title: Daybench: quant + prompt sweep scratchpad
content:
Quick running log for the Daybench micro-eval: messy, actionable bits.

Context / goal:
- Reduce inference cost on 13B-sized model family while preserving chat-quality for our customer-facing chat routes. Target: <= 0.8 quality regression (relative) on core prompt set, 2x token/sec improvement on dedicated T4-like nodes, and stable KV-cache behavior for 1k prefix tokens.
- Trying PTQ + dynamic range calibrations + a small prompt-rewrite experiment (few-shot -> single-shot with exemplar compression).

Notes 2026-03-10 AM run:
- Baseline: fp16 native on dev-node-a: 13B, seq=1024, batch=1: 210 tokens/s, p50 latency 290ms.
- Int8 PTQ (symmetric per-tensor) via quant-sim v0.9: 380 tokens/s, p50 170ms, but BLEU-ish style eval (prompt-set-A) dropped ~9% absolute on Answer-Fidelity metric (from 0.82 -> 0.73).
- Int8 + KV cache warm: when running repeated prefixes model behaves fine up to 512 prefix; beyond that >10% divergence in sampling occasionally (investigate rounding in KV writes).

Things to test next (high priority):
- [ ] Run per-channel quant (per-out) with calibration on 1k calibration steps from dataset "convo-mini-v2". Hypothesis: reduce fidelity drop to <5%.
- [ ] Try QAT-lite (simulate quant noise during fine-tune) for 500 steps at lr=1e-5 on distilled prompt-set (small). Budget: 2 TPU-hours.
- [ ] Re-run streaming sampling check with deterministic seeds on quant model to pin down when sampling divergence occurs (is it deterministic or data-dependent?).

Prompt-set notes (quick):
- prompt-set-A: 120 evaluation prompts (customer support + code completion mix). Seeds 1001-1120.
- prompt-set-B: 40 adversarial prompts (long context + conflicting instructions).
- Compression experiment: take 3 exemplar shots -> single-shot with compressed summary (LLM summarize 3->1). Early spot-checks show latency reduction but slight drop in specificity on knowledge-heavy prompts.

Microbench table (hand notes):
- fp16   | batch1 | seq1024 | 210 t/s | p50 290ms | QF 0.82
- int8   | batch1 | seq1024 | 380 t/s | p50 170ms | QF 0.73
- int8-pc| batch1 | seq1024 | 360 t/s | p50 185ms | QF 0.79 (per-channel approx)

Calibration plan (short):
- Use 5k tokens sampled from convo-mini-v2 (mix of short/long).
- Save activations for attention + FFN layers. Run per-channel symmetric quantization with outlier clipping at 99.9 percentile.
- Evaluate layerwise MSE and rank layers by worst-case error. Likely culprits: FFN projection out, final LM head.

Open questions / brain-dump:
- Is our quant library doing fused KV writes with lower precision for cache storage? If yes, need to verify read-path casting. Patch idea: store cached keys in fp16 even if compute in int8, to avoid compounding rounding.
- Does the runtime's kernel-selection fallback change for per-channel kernels? Some micro-schedule choices might disable attention-fuse causing perf regressions. Check kernel trace logs.
- For prompt-compression: when we compress exemplars, are we inadvertently removing rare tokens that serve as anchors for retrieval-style answers? Might need to add anchor tokens back.

Quick TODOs (today):
- [ ] Start per-channel calibration run on dev-gpu-7 (ticket JIRA-ML-519). Command: ./quantize --model path/to/13b --calib convo-mini-v2 --mode per-channel --clip 0.999
- [ ] Add logging to KV write path: include dtype stored, shape, and checksum. Lightweight patch, push to draft PR.
- [ ] Run deterministic eval on prompt-set-B with seed 42 for all quant variants and save outputs under outputs/daybench/2026-03-10/.

Experiment notes (heuristics):
- If per-channel brings QF delta <= 4% and perf > 1.6x: candidate for rollout to dedicated.
- If we hit divergence on repeated prefixes despite fp16 storage: consider asymmetrical quant for KV store (use int8 for compute, fp16 for cache persist).

References / snippets:
- Quick snippet I used for sampling test: seed=42; temperature=0.2; top_p=0.95; streaming=true; measure tokens/s from runtime tracing (trace_id: daybench-03-10-run1).
- GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/842 (adds KV debug logging).
- Confluence: detailed eval checklist at CONFLUENCE-1234 (private).

Misc notes to self:
- Keep runs small and reproducible. Use same hardware or note node id.
- When reporting to Maya/Arjun, include token/sec, p50, QF metric, and a single example where model changed answer (diff). They like the diff-first approach.

End-of-day state: rough wins but still too noisy. Prioritize per-channel calibration and KV-storage dtype fix.
